paragraphs: BibliU sells a course materials platform to colleges and universities, automating the workflow behind digital textbooks and courseware. It also runs campus stores, pairing that content with physical and online retail.

The platform comes in three named parts: Learn, Engage and Automate. Faculty choose titles and adaptive courseware from thousands of publishers and open educational resources, so the selection stays with academics. The company says the access model cuts textbook costs by 30 to 50 percent. Students can read on any device, online or off. Staff get reporting that tracks content usage and student engagement. A separate procurement option is built for libraries, with flexible pricing and broad title access.

The site says more than 170 institutions worldwide use the company. Dual credit students are called out as one group served, with the same first-day access to required materials. Dave Sherwood is co-founder and chief executive. He started the company while at Oxford University. A case studies page collects customer stories from across higher education.

quote.text: The future of higher education is about ensuring all students have affordable access to their class content.
